newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: National caucus ready to defer tax cuts - Eve Post.
newsitem.headline: National caucus ready to defer tax cuts - Eve Post.

text.p: The National Party caucus meeting on Wednesday endorsed a coalition agreement with New Zealand First, the Evening Post newspaper reported on Thursday.
The newspaper reported National MP Nick Smith saying the meeting of MPs was relaxed about postponing next year's planned tax cuts as the price of a coalition deal.

"I think the mood of the caucus is one of acceptance of the package that has been put forward by the negotiating team and that if that pulls off a coalition deal with NZ First, that is well and good," Smith said.
National has already passed the $1.1 billion in cuts into law, but NZ First wants more spending and the tax cuts diverted into a compulsory superannuation scheme.

Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash last month warned the cuts might have to be deferred if net government spending increased. He said the two together would threaten the bank's 0-2 percent inflation target.
MPs contacted by Reuters were more equivocal about how far the caucus went in giving the negotiating team the go-ahead.

National Party sources said strong words were exchanged at the caucus, but they differed on how much agreement had been reached. One MP close to the negotiations said there had been a "full and frank discussion".

"It is a long and complex process. We have still got some distance to go in terms of exposing the full array of issues to the caucus," the MP said, adding the caucus had not given the deal final approval.
A National backbencher confirmed a range of views were expressed at the caucus, but on only scant detail of the shape of a deal.
Meanwhile no formal coalition negotiations have been set down for Thursday, a NZ First spokeman said.
But Labour employment spokesman Steve Maharey and NZ First policy coordinator Peter McCardle held a brief face to face meeting in the morning.

In the early afternoon NZ First leader Winston Peters, his brother and legal adviser to NZ First Wayne Peters and Labour negotiator Mike Moore had a highly-visible lunch together at a table on the footpath outside Paris restaurant on Lambton Quay.

Nationalist NZ First holds the balance of power after the October 12 election and is negotiating separately with both the caretaker conservative National government and centre-left Labour over the shape of the new government.
NZ First MPs are confident a final decision can be made before parliament sits next week.
